Written by this library from the prose of the W3C Recommendation Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE (REC-vc-jose-cose-20250515), which prints no JSON Schema, CDDL or ABNF of its own. Source .cache/w3c-vc-jose-cose.bin, sha256 6c70cf8d7de9d8a3ff28a743fea9d569a67a402111c3245fdafbaa2ad6709af9; quotations of the source are checked against its rendering .cache/w3c-vc-jose-cose.txt, sha256 f02bd4966800863d533746c6c39ad267ada1b8bfcbb92186c204b617bb46c126. Quotations of other documents are checked against the copies README.md lists with their digests. INSTANCE: an EnvelopedVerifiableCredential object (#vc), an EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation object (#vp), or a bare data: URL string (#data-uri-vc, #data-uri-vp, #data-url). LEVELS. The root and every anchor not ending in -should state MUST and MUST NOT rules: a failure is non-conformance. A rule marked imported is a MUST of another document, named with the clause of this source that makes it bind. Anchors ending in -should add the SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED and NOT RECOMMENDED statements and include the MUST level by reference: a failure there is a deviation from a recommendation, to be reported as a warning, never as non-conformance. A constraint marked inferred is a reading this library made, not a statement of the source. SHOULD level: #data-uri-vc-should, #data-uri-vp-should. What is checked is the shape of the object and of its data: URL; the secured object inside is checked by decoding the data and applying jose-header, payload, sd-jwt or cose-sign1 by its media type (README.md, How to apply).
title: EnvelopedVerifiableCredential / EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation and their data: URLs (DERIVED)

envelopedVc.description: An EnvelopedVerifiableCredential object, as this source requires it and as VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.13 defines it.

@context.$comment: imported: “The @context property of the object MUST be present and include a context, such as the base context for this specification, that defines at least the id, type, and EnvelopedVerifiableCredential terms as defined by the base context provided by this specification.” (VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.13) Presence and shape are checked; whether the context defines the id, type and EnvelopedVerifiableCredential terms needs JSON-LD processing and is not checked.

id.$comment: imported: “The id value of the object MUST be a data: URL [RFC2397] that expresses a secured verifiable credential using an enveloping security scheme, such as Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE [VC-JOSE-COSE].” (VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.13)

type.$comment: “Verifiable Credentials secured in verifiable presentations MUST use the Enveloped Verifiable Credential type defined by the [VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0].” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0021); w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0037; w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0057. imported: “The type value of the object MUST be EnvelopedVerifiableCredential.” (VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.13) A one-element array is accepted (inferred: JSON-LD reads ["EnvelopedVerifiableCredential"] and "EnvelopedVerifiableCredential" alike, and Example 2's Presentation view prints the array); an array with further types is not.

envelopedVc.$comment: MUST level. Credentials in a presentation must also be secured (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0023, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0039, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0059): an enveloped credential is secured when its id is a data: URL of a secured credential. This object checks the shape of that URL; the secured object inside is checked by decoding it and applying jose-header, sd-jwt or cose-sign1 by its media type (cross-field-rules.derived.yaml X-10). The second sentence of each, “In this case, these credentials are secured using JWS.” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0023) and its SD-JWT and COSE twins, is not enforced: Examples 8, 20 and 23 enclose credentials secured otherwise (README.md, Findings).

id.$comment: imported: “The id value of the object MUST be a data: URL [RFC2397] that expresses a secured verifiable presentation using an enveloping securing mechanism, such as Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE [VC-JOSE-COSE].” (VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.13)

type.$comment: “Verifiable Presentations in verifiable presentations MUST use the Enveloped Verifiable Presentation type defined by the [VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0].” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0022); w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0038; w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0058. imported: “The type value of the object MUST be EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation.” (VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.13) A one-element array is accepted (inferred: JSON-LD reads ["EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation"] and "EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation" alike, and Example 2's Presentation view prints the array); an array with further types is not.

envelopedVp.$comment: MUST level. The source names no member of a presentation that holds another presentation (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0022 and its twins); Examples 3, 6 and 9 secure an EnvelopedVerifiablePresentation as the payload itself, and payload.derived.schema.json applies this object there.

allOf.$comment: imported: “The id value of the object MUST be a data: URL [RFC2397] that expresses a secured verifiable credential using an enveloping security scheme, such as Securing Verifiable Credentials using JOSE and COSE [VC-JOSE-COSE].” (VC-DATA-MODEL-2.0 §4.13), named by the Enveloped type rules (README.md, How the imports bind). The pattern is RFC 2397 §3, “dataurl := "data:" [ mediatype ] [ ";base64" ] "," data” (RFC 2397 §3), as a regular expression; data-uri.derived.abnf is the same grammar in ABNF. data is read as RFC 2396 uric, after “where "urlchar" is imported from [RFC2396]” (RFC 2397 §3), and RFC 2396 defines no rule of that name (inferred). A parameter needs an =, by “The ";base64" extension is distinguishable from a content-type parameter by the fact that it doesn't have a following "=" sign.” (RFC 2397 §3), so ;base64url, a space, or a quoted parameter value fails here. The scheme and ;base64 compare case-insensitively (inferred), and so does the media type: “Both top-level type and subtype names are case-insensitive.” (RFC 6838 §4.2).

inferred: the object carries a secured credential, so a media type of the other kind (application/vp+...) fails. The kind of each media type is read off the normative section that recommends it as a typ value: vc+jwt, vc+sd-jwt and application/vc+cose in the credential sections §3.1.1, §3.2.1 and §3.3.1 (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0013, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0028, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0048), vp+jwt, vp+sd-jwt and application/vp+cose in the presentation sections §3.1.2, §3.2.2 and §3.3.2 (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0018, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0034, w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0054). The §6.1 registrations (inline.verbatim.txt I-01 to I-06) say the same, in a section marked non-normative, and ground nothing.

application/vc+jwt: the data is a JWS in the Compact Serialization, three non-empty base64url segments joined by periods, or (RFC 2397 permits it; the source neither shows nor forbids it) the base64 encoding of one. Inferred: §5.1, which is normative, takes vc+jwt and vp+jwt as an input document secured as a JWT [RFC7519] (inline.verbatim.txt I-08; it names only a credential, SD-18), RFC 7519 §1 says “JWTs are always represented using the JWS Compact Serialization or the JWE Compact Serialization.” (RFC 7519 §1), and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0012 and its twin say a JWS issuer MUST use [RFC7515] to secure the media type, so the JWT is a JWS, and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0025 requires its compact serialization to be supported. The §6.1 registration says the same (for credentials: “This specification registers the application/vc+jwt Media Type specifically for identifying a JSON Web Token (JWT) with a payload conforming to the Verifiable Credential Data Model.” (§6.1.1)), in a section marked non-normative, so it corroborates and grounds nothing. A JWE (five segments, the nesting w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0016 and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0024 allow) fails: the source does not say what media type the encrypted form takes. An empty signature segment, the unsecured form, fails, by w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0005 and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0023. A doubled value such as <JWS>;data:application/vc+jwt,<JWS> has a valid RFC 2397 shape and fails here (Examples 2, 3 and 20).

application/vc+sd-jwt: an SD-JWT or SD-JWT+KB in the compact serialization, by the ABNF of RFC 9901 §4 (imported through w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0027; the source cites [SD-JWT] as an Internet-Draft with no revision, C.1, and RFC 9901 is its published form), or its base64 encoding as for JWT. w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0042 requires compact support; the source's own words: “If the KB-JWT is not present, the SD-JWT must end with a tilde (~) character.” (§1.1.2.2). A KB-JWT followed by a further tilde matches neither form and fails (Example 22).

MUST: “When including verifiable credentials secured with COSE in verifiable presentations as Enveloped Verifiable Credentials, the credentials MUST be encoded using base64 as specified in [RFC2397].” (w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0051). RFC 2397 §2: “The appearance of ";base64" means that the data is encoded as base64.” (RFC 2397 §2) The data is held to the base64 alphabet of RFC 2045 §6.8, padded to a multiple of four characters, with no line break inside the URL (inferred). data:application/vc+cose;base64url,... fails: base64url is neither the RFC 2397 extension nor a parameter (Example 20).

dataUriVc.$comment: Media type parameters (attribute=value, as RFC 2397 section 3 writes mediatype) are admitted at the MUST and SHOULD levels alike, before ;base64 and the comma. The §6.1 templates list none (their Required parameters and Optional parameters rows, inline.verbatim.txt I-01 to I-06), but §6 is marked non-normative, so it grounds no level here (README.md, Requirement levels).

dataUriVcShould.$comment: SHOULD level, inferred: w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0008 and w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0009 ask that media types distinguish verifiable credentials and that the most specific one be used, and the data: URL's media type is where an enveloped object carries one. A data: URL with no media type, or with application/jwt, application/sd-jwt or another generic type, deviates here. A media type of another enveloping scheme deviates too; the unless clause of w3c-vc-jose-cose#R-0010 leaves room for one that identifies the format better, which this schema cannot know of.

dataUrl.$comment: RFC 2397 §3 alone, any media type (data-uri.derived.abnf, rule dataurl).
